l4_steps.name: Ingest airman certificate data from FAA IACRA
l4_steps.system: FAA IACRA (Integrated Airman Certification and Rating Application)
l4_steps.input: Scheduled nightly sync trigger from FAA IACRA API
l4_steps.output: Refreshed airman certificate dataset with ATP, type rating, and medical records
l4_steps.kpi: Data sync completion rate ≥99.5%; sync latency <4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA IACRA API throttling during peak batch windows causes stale cert data; no real-time push — polling-only model creates up to 24-hour lag for urgent status changes

l4_steps.name: Risk-rank crew by certification expiry proximity
l4_steps.input: Refreshed IACRA certificate dataset; crew scheduling horizon (90-day window)
l4_steps.output: Risk-ranked crew list: Red (expiry <30 days), Amber (30–60 days), Green (>60 days)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of crew with expiry <30 days flagged Red; zero missed flags
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen CM risk-ranking logic does not account for Special Issuance (SI) medical conditions with shorter validity windows, causing under-flagging of affected crew

l4_steps.name: Issue automated crew renewal notification
l4_steps.input: Risk-ranked crew list with Red/Amber flags
l4_steps.output: Automated email and in-app notification to crew member and Chief Pilot with renewal deadlines and action links
l4_steps.kpi: Notification delivery rate ≥99%; crew acknowledgement within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew members on extended international layovers or LOA may miss email alerts; no SMS or push notification fallback in current Jeppesen CM configuration

l4_steps.name: Submit MedXpress application for AME examination
l4_steps.input: Crew renewal notification; upcoming medical certificate expiry date
l4_steps.output: Completed FAA Form 8500-8 application submitted to designated AME; confirmation number issued
l4_steps.kpi: MedXpress submission completed ≥21 days before certificate expiry
l4_steps.pain_point: MedXpress portal outages during FAA system maintenance windows block submission; crew booking AME appointments within <14 days of expiry creates duty-coverage gaps

l4_steps.name: Conduct Class 1 AME physical examination
l4_steps.input: FAA Form 8500-8; crew member presenting at AME office
l4_steps.output: Completed physical examination; AME determination recorded in MedXpress
l4_steps.kpi: First-attempt Class 1 pass rate ≥92%; examination cycle time <2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Age-40 rule requires captains over 40 to hold Class 1 medical renewed every 6 months (vs. 12 months under 40), doubling administrative burden for senior captain cohort; resource-intensive for AME network

l4_steps.name: Validate medical certificate against FAR Part 67
l4_steps.input: AME examination result and MedXpress determination
l4_steps.output: Medical certificate issued (valid) or Special Issuance referral / denial issued
l4_steps.kpi: Validation processing time <24 hours post-examination; Special Issuance cases escalated within 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 67 Special Issuance (SI) for conditions such as hypertension or AASM-treated OSA requires FAA Regional Flight Surgeon review averaging 30–90 days, creating extended grounding risk for borderline cases

l4_steps.name: Upload validated medical certificate to crew record
l4_steps.input: Issued FAA First-Class medical certificate PDF; validation confirmation from MedXpress
l4_steps.output: Updated crew qualification record in Jeppesen CM with new medical expiry date; scheduling constraints lifted
l4_steps.kpi: Record update latency <2 hours post-certificate issue; zero scheduling errors attributable to stale medical data
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual PDF upload to Jeppesen CM creates transcription error risk; no automated IACRA-to-Jeppesen integration for medical records means dual-entry is required

l4_steps.name: Query aircraft type rating currency in Jeppesen CM
l4_steps.input: Updated crew record; assigned aircraft type (B737-700 / B737-800 / B737 MAX 8)
l4_steps.output: Type rating currency report showing rating issue date, expiry, and recency event log
l4_steps.kpi: Query response time <30 seconds; currency data accuracy ≥99.9% vs. FAA IACRA record
l4_steps.pain_point: B737 MAX 8 return-to-service post-2020 grounding introduced new FCTM differences training requirement tracked outside standard type rating schema in Jeppesen CM, causing manual gap-check overhead

l4_steps.name: Verify FAR 61.57 recency requirements for flight ops
l4_steps.input: Type rating currency report; recent flight log data from crew tracking module
l4_steps.output: Recency compliance determination: compliant or lapsed for each currency category (takeoff/landing, IFR, PIC)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of crew checked for recency currency before schedule publication; zero recency violations detected post-assignment
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 61.57(d) instrument currency requires 6 approaches in 6 months; crew returning from extended medical leave frequently have lapsed IFR currency not flagged until check-in, requiring last-minute schedule swaps

l4_steps.name: Schedule simulator proficiency check for lapsed recency
l4_steps.input: Recency lapse determination; simulator availability calendar
l4_steps.output: Simulator proficiency check event booked in Jeppesen CM; crew notified with date, location, and evaluator
l4_steps.kpi: Simulator slot secured within 10 business days of recency lapse identified; no-show rate <3%
l4_steps.pain_point: Simulator capacity at airline training centres is shared with initial qualification training; short-notice recency check bookings are frequently bumped, extending grounding duration and creating crew shortage risk on high-frequency routes

l4_steps.name: Cross-reference certificates with FAA IACRA Airmen Inquiry
l4_steps.system: FAA IACRA (Integrated Airman Certification and Rating Application)
l4_steps.input: Crew qualification records from Jeppesen CM; FAA certificate numbers
l4_steps.output: IACRA cross-reference report confirming or flagging discrepancies in ATP, type rating, and medical certificate status
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of active crew cross-referenced monthly; discrepancy detection rate >95% vs. manual audit
l4_steps.pain_point: IACRA Airmen Inquiry public API does not expose enforcement action flags or certificate surrender status in real time; airlines must rely on PRIA (Pilot Records Improvement Act) database for hiring but have no automated ongoing pull for current employees

l4_steps.name: Verify Special Issuance conditions and SODA exemptions
l4_steps.input: IACRA cross-reference report; crew medical history flags; FAA SI letter on file
l4_steps.output: SI compliance verification: conditions met, or deviation requiring FAA Regional Flight Surgeon follow-up identified
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of crew with active SI conditions reviewed quarterly; zero SI deadline breaches
l4_steps.pain_point: Special Issuance conditions (e.g., post-cardiac event, CPAP therapy compliance) carry individual FAA-imposed timelines and monitoring requirements; tracking these in a generic crew management system without structured SI workflow fields leads to missed review deadlines

l4_steps.name: Update crew qualification matrix with verified certifications
l4_steps.input: IACRA cross-reference report; SI compliance verification; proficiency check results
l4_steps.output: Fully updated crew qualification matrix; scheduling system reflects current authorised aircraft types and positions
l4_steps.kpi: Qualification matrix updated within 4 hours of verification completion; scheduling system sync lag <1 hour
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualification matrix updates in Jeppesen CM do not automatically propagate to codeshare partner crew systems, requiring manual data exchange for any interline or wet-lease arrangements

l4_steps.name: Flag non-compliant crew and initiate grounding hold
l4_steps.input: Compliance failure flag from certification validation or IACRA cross-reference
l4_steps.output: Grounding hold applied in Jeppesen CM; crew member status set to NOT QUALIFIED; Chief Pilot and Crew Scheduling notified
l4_steps.kpi: Grounding hold applied within 2 hours of compliance failure detection; zero non-compliant crew departing on scheduled flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Grounding holds in Jeppesen CM do not automatically trigger crew pay adjustment workflow in SAP SuccessFactors; manual payroll correction required for grounded crew on paid leave status, creating HR disputes

l4_steps.name: Remove crew from active schedule and source replacement
l4_steps.input: Grounding hold notification; affected flight assignments; available reserve crew list
l4_steps.output: Affected flights reassigned or covered by reserve crew; operational disruption minimised
l4_steps.kpi: Replacement crew sourced within 3 hours of grounding notification; schedule disruption rate <1% attributable to certification grounding
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve crew pools sized for weather/irregular operations events — simultaneous grounding of multiple crew for certification non-compliance (e.g., post-audit sweep) can exhaust reserve capacity on thin-coverage focus city stations

l4_steps.name: Track remediation progress and certification renewal
l4_steps.input: Grounding hold record; crew member self-reported remediation milestones; AME/simulator confirmations
l4_steps.output: Remediation tracking log with milestone dates; estimated return-to-duty date communicated to Crew Scheduling
l4_steps.kpi: Average grounding duration <14 days for medical renewal cases; <7 days for recency cases
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen CM has no structured remediation workflow module; compliance analysts track grounding cases in spreadsheets outside the system, creating audit trail gaps and no automated escalation if remediation stalls beyond SLA

l4_steps.name: Restore crew to active status and release scheduling block
l4_steps.input: Confirmed certification compliance from remediation tracking; updated qualification matrix
l4_steps.output: Grounding hold lifted; crew status restored to QUALIFIED; crew available for scheduling from next bid period or immediate standby
l4_steps.kpi: Reinstatement processing time <2 hours after compliance confirmed; zero scheduling errors on reinstatement day
l4_steps.pain_point: Reinstatement requires manual dual-approval (Crew Compliance Manager + Chief Pilot) with no digital workflow; paper sign-off process creates delays when approvers are on-duty in different time zones

l4_steps.name: Generate certification compliance dashboard in Tableau
l4_steps.input: Qualification matrix export from Jeppesen CM; grounding event log; remediation tracking data
l4_steps.output: Live certification compliance dashboard showing fleet-wide expiry profile, grounding incidents, and trend lines by certificate type
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard refresh latency <4 hours; fleet-wide certification compliance rate KPI target ≥99.0%
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau dashboard relies on manual Jeppesen CM data exports rather than live API feed; stale data during audits or regulatory inspections undermines credibility with FAA Principal Operations Inspector (POI)

l4_steps.name: Export FAA regulatory audit package and file deviations
l4_steps.input: Certification compliance dashboard; grounding and reinstatement event log; corrective action records
l4_steps.output: Regulatory audit package (PDF + CSV) ready for FAA POI review; deviation reports filed via ASAP program if compliance threshold breached
l4_steps.kpi: Audit package prepared within 24 hours of FAA request; zero open compliance findings older than 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Aviation Safety Action Program (ASAP) event reporting for certification deviations is voluntary and narrative-based; without structured data capture in Jeppesen CM, root cause trending across deviation events requires labour-intensive manual analysis
